stories.headline: Tesla starts early Optimus production on Fremont's high-volume line, cuts 2026 capex to ~$20B

key_facts.fact: Tesla's Q3 2026 update (Oct 21) says Optimus production began in Fremont on high-volume lines, calling the units 'the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured'.
key_facts.excerpt: Optimus production began in Fremont on our high-volume lines. The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured. While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product.

key_facts.fact: Tesla's capacity table lists Optimus in California as 'Early Ramp' and a second Optimus site in Texas as under construction.
key_facts.excerpt: Robotics | California | Optimus | - | Early Ramp | Texas | Optimus | - | Construction

key_facts.fact: Musk called it 'early production' with a slow, 'somewhat bumpy' ramp, and claimed Tesla will be able to make 20,000 robots per week by the end of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk said on a conference call that he considers this "early production" and that the ramp will be slow and "somewhat bumpy because it is such a radically new product." He nonetheless claimed Tesla will be able to make 20,000 of them per week by the end of 2027.

key_facts.fact: Musk said the robot's hands are not yet perfected, that Tesla expects to start delivering Optimus to outside companies around end-2027, and that it hopes to put its AI5 chip (about 10x AI4's compute) into Optimus around April 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: "We're building robots that do not have perfected hands," he said... Musk said he hopes to put the company's AI5 chip into Optimus around April 2027, providing roughly 10 times the computing power of AI4.

key_facts.fact: Musk said Tesla needs to build roughly 10,000 to 20,000 robots to practice tasks at an 'Optimus Academy' because, unlike cars, it has no installed fleet to gather training data from.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk said Tesla therefore needs to build roughly 10,000 to 20,000 robots to practice tasks at what he called "Optimus Academy."

key_facts.fact: Tesla cut its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to roughly $20 billion from more than $25 billion; Q3 capex was $4.7 billion versus the $7.5 billion analysts expected.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla said it expected capital expenses for 2026 to be roughly $20 billion, down from its previous forecast of more than $25 billion... Tesla spent $4.7 billion in capex, double that of a year ago, but lower than the $7.5 billion analysts on average were expecting

key_facts.fact: Tesla's Q3 net income fell 43% year over year to $787 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The company reported $787 million in net income, a 43% drop from the same period in 2025, when it earned $1.37 billion.

stories.headline: Micron union stages Taiwan's first-ever chip-industry strike over AI-profit sharing

key_facts.fact: A Micron labor union in Taoyuan staged Taiwan's first-ever strike in the semiconductor industry on Thursday, Oct. 22, in a dispute over how AI-boom windfall profits are shared.
key_facts.excerpt: TAIPEI -- A Micron Technology labor union staged Taiwan's first-ever strike in the semiconductor industry on Thursday as part of a dispute over how huge windfall profits from the artificial intelligence boom are shared.

key_facts.fact: Talks on Oct. 21 between Micron Taiwan chairman Lu Dong-hui and the Taoyuan union ended without consensus; the union said 11 union officers would strike from 9 a.m. Oct. 22 to 9 a.m. Oct. 23.
key_facts.excerpt: 美光21日下午由台灣美光董事長盧東暉等人持續與桃園工會代表進行協商，只是雙方並未達成共識... 11名工會幹部將於今天上午9時至23日上午9時進行罷工。

key_facts.fact: Only a handful of workers joined the walkout, although more than 2,000 Taoyuan employees had planned to stop work; talks were set to resume on Oct. 23.
key_facts.excerpt: Five of the striking Micron workers gathered outside the Taoyuan plant... More than 2,000 employees at the Taoyuan plant had planned to stop working on Oct 22... He added that talks with the US firm would continue on Oct 23.

key_facts.fact: The unions seek an 83-month bonus and a permanent system giving workers 15% of operating profits; Micron's September offer of up to 68 months of pay as a one-off was rejected.
key_facts.excerpt: the unions seek an 83-month bonus and a permanent system giving workers 15% of operating profits... Micron... said in September it would give the equivalent of up to 68 months of pay to staff but the one-off payment was rejected by workers.

key_facts.fact: Micron said its deal with the separate Taichung union moves to a quarterly profit-sharing bonus and raises pension contributions; the Taoyuan union condemned it as a unilateral agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron had agreed to move to a quarterly profit-sharing bonus system and increase the company's pension contribution, Lu said on Oct 22... "They instead reached a unilateral agreement with the Taichung union. We strongly condemn this," he added.

key_facts.fact: Micron makes around 50% to 60% of its chips in Taiwan, where it produces DRAM and high-bandwidth memory for AI servers.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron, which makes around 50% to 60% of its chips in Taiwan

stories.headline: Lam Research posts record $8.22B quarter; TI revenue jumps 28% with data center up ~95%

key_facts.fact: Lam Research reported record September-quarter revenue of $8.22 billion, up 22% from June, with GAAP EPS of $2.19 and an operating margin of 40.0%.
key_facts.excerpt: For the September 2026 quarter, revenue was $8.22 billion, gross margin was $4.30 billion, or 52.3% of revenue... operating margin was 40.0%, and net income was $2.75 billion, or $2.19 per diluted share

key_facts.fact: China was Lam's largest market at 35% of revenue, and Lam guided December-quarter revenue to $8.60 billion plus or minus $400 million.
key_facts.excerpt: China 35 % Korea 20 % Taiwan 18 %... Revenue $8.60 Billion +/- $400 Million

key_facts.fact: Lam's revenue rose 54% year over year; memory systems revenue hit a record, up 120% from a year earlier, with NAND revenue up about 40% sequentially.
key_facts.excerpt: September quarter revenue was $8.22 billion, which was up 22% sequentially and up 54% from the same period in 2025... On a dollar basis, this represented a record level for memory, and it was up 120%... NAND revenue increased approximately 40% sequentially

key_facts.fact: Despite the record, Lam shares fell 6.82% after hours to $243.01.
key_facts.excerpt: Lam Research (LRCX) | $260.81 | -1.00% | Record revenue; -6.82% after hours to $243.01

key_facts.fact: Texas Instruments reported Q3 revenue of $6.06 billion, up 28% year over year, net income of $2.43 billion and EPS of $2.62, and guided Q4 revenue to $5.80-$6.30 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Texas Instruments Incorporated (TI) (Nasdaq: TXN) today reported third quarter revenue of $6.06 billion, net income of $2.43 billion and earnings per share of $2.62... TI's fourth quarter outlook is for revenue in the range of $5.80 billion to $6.30 billion

key_facts.fact: TI said data center revenue grew about 95% year over year and about 20% sequentially, reaching 13% of company revenue; industrial grew more than 40%.
key_facts.excerpt: Data Center Revenue -- growing approximately 95% year over year and representing 13% of total company revenue... Data center was up about 95% year-on-year and grew about 20% sequentially.

stories.headline: Security firm Lava traces 32 banned Nvidia B300 chips to China Telecom-linked IP addresses

key_facts.fact: Israeli security company Lava found 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips connected to systems linked to state-owned China Telecom, despite US export controls; The Information reported it on Oct. 22.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's Powerful B300 Chips Spotted on Chinese State-Owned Network

key_facts.fact: Lava traced the chips through publicly exposed instances of Nvidia's DCGM Exporter GPU-monitoring tool; the exposed endpoints revealed the hardware and IP addresses pointing to China Telecom.
key_facts.excerpt: Lava traced the chips through publicly exposed instances of Nvidia's DCGM Exporter. This is a monitoring tool that operators use to keep tabs on their GPUs... the hardware included 32 B300 chips, and the associated IP addresses pointed back to China Telecom.

key_facts.fact: The finding is a network association with the carrier's IP addresses, not confirmation of who physically owns the hardware or where it sits, and nothing indicates Nvidia itself sold the chips into China.
key_facts.excerpt: Lava's work links the chips to IP addresses connected to the carrier. That is a network association, and it is a different thing from confirming who physically owns the hardware or exactly where it sits... Nothing in Lava's findings indicates Nvidia itself sold the chips into China.

key_facts.fact: The discovery builds on an Oct. 9 Lava study that found about 2,100 exposed DCGM Exporter hosts worldwide and flagged an Nvidia vulnerability, CVE-2026-47483, rated 8.2.
key_facts.excerpt: Lava identified approximately 2,100 exposed DCGM Exporter hosts globally in that earlier work. The same report flagged a vulnerability in Nvidia's systems tracked as CVE-2026-47483. It carries a severity rating of 8.2

key_facts.fact: The B300 sits under the strictest US control for China, a presumption of license denial, while the older H200 moved to case-by-case review in January.
key_facts.excerpt: The B300, a Blackwell Ultra part, sits under the strictest US control, a presumption of license denial for China, while the older H200 moved to case-by-case review in January

stories.headline: Huang says he told Nscale to 'work around the clock'; neoclouds 'just need working capital'

key_facts.fact: At a GTC Berlin press conference on Thursday, Oct. 22, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he told Nvidia-backed UK neocloud Nscale to 'work around the clock' to bring delayed data centers online.
key_facts.excerpt: "Come, you guys, do a good job, work around the clock," Huang recalled telling the company, speaking during a press conference on Thursday. "That was it."

key_facts.fact: Nscale has faced delays, equipment failures and power constraints at some sites, plus investor pushback over its $30 billion IPO valuation target.
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale... has been grappling with delays, equipment failures and power constraints at some of its data center sites as well as investor pushback over its $30 billion IPO valuation target.

key_facts.fact: Huang said neoclouds will overcome their problems because 'they have excellent customers, demand is really high, and they just need working capital'.
key_facts.excerpt: "I'm quite confident that they will find solutions, and their solution starts with the fact that they have excellent customers, demand is really high, and they just need working capital," Huang said

key_facts.fact: Huang said data centers once took three years to build, but 'now, if you don't get it up and running in six months, everybody's up in arms.'
key_facts.excerpt: Historically, infrastructure companies could take three years to build a data center. "Now, if you don't get it up and running in six months, everybody's up in arms."

key_facts.fact: The remarks follow recent neocloud stumbles: Australia's Firmus Grid abandoned a $30 billion IPO and South Korea's Elice had a difficult trading debut, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index suffered its longest losing streak since 2008.
key_facts.excerpt: Australian company Firmus Grid, one of the many Nvidia-backed neoclouds, abandoned a $30 billion IPO in Australia and South Korea's Elice had a difficult trading debut... the closely watched Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index suffered its longest losing streak since 2008.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft withdrew from a £2 billion Nscale project in Loughton, Essex, after grid-connection delays pushed the site's availability into the 2030s; it would have housed 23,040 Nvidia GB300 GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft has withdrawn from a £2 billion UK project there with Nscale after delays in power grid connections pushed the site's availability into the 2030s. That project would have housed 23,040 Nvidia GB300 GPUs.

stories.headline: Nebius signs as first customer for HUMAIN and DataVolt's AI campus at NEOM's Oxagon

key_facts.fact: On Oct. 21, Saudi PIF company HUMAIN and DataVolt announced a preliminary framework agreement with Nebius for data center capacity at Oxagon, NEOM's industrial city on the Red Sea coast.
key_facts.excerpt: HUMAIN, the PIF company delivering full-stack artificial intelligence capabilities globally, and DataVolt... today announced a preliminary framework agreement with Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS), a leading AI cloud company, for data center capacity at Oxagon

key_facts.fact: Nebius would be anchor customer, with up to 50 MW of offtake: half of the initial 100 MW under construction, part of a first phase planned at 360 MW.
key_facts.excerpt: Nebius would become an anchor customer for the planned AI giga campus, with the contemplated offtake representing up to 50MW (half of the initial 100 MW currently under construction as part of the first phase's planned 360 MW.)

key_facts.fact: The capacity is expected to come online in phases from Q4 2027, and Nebius is expected to deploy Nvidia-powered infrastructure there.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed capacity allocation is expected to become operational in phases from Q4 2027... with Nebius expected to deploy NVIDIA-powered computing infrastructure under the agreement

key_facts.fact: The deal was signed on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC Berlin, six weeks after construction began; HUMAIN CEO Tareq Amin called Nebius its first customer.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nebius agreement, signed on the sidelines of NVIDIA's GTC Berlin conference... just six weeks after announcing the commencement of construction... "Advancing our commercial relationship with Nebius as our first customer is a significant milestone for HUMAIN"

sources.title: HUMAIN and DataVolt advance AI infrastructure framework with Nebius for planned giga campus in NEOM's Oxagon

stories.headline: Robotics startups Enact and Maxinsights each raise $30M; Mensch and LeCun back Enact

key_facts.fact: Swiss startup Enact Intelligence emerged from stealth on Oct. 22 with a $30 million pre-seed round to build full-stack technology for general-purpose robots.
key_facts.excerpt: Swiss robotics startup Enact Intelligence has today emerged out of stealth, with a $30m pre-seed round... Enact is building the underlying technology for general purpose robots.

key_facts.fact: Investors include Redalpine, Notion Capital and Firstminute Capital, plus angels Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch, Yann LeCun and Hugging Face's Thomas Wolf.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors in the round include Redalpine, Notion Capital and Firstminute Capital, with angel investors including Mensch, LeCun and Hugging Face's Thomas Wolf.

key_facts.fact: Enact's robots sense force and touch through their own actuators rather than relying mainly on cameras; CEO Manuel Yves Galliker previously worked at Physical Intelligence.
key_facts.excerpt: Manuel Yves Galliker, its CEO and co-founder, who previously worked at the hot US robotics startup Physical Intelligence, said: "In particular, our robots sense force and touch through their own actuators, so they feel what's happening in real time"

key_facts.fact: Maxinsights, which creates robot training data from first-person footage captured by cameras worn by more than 5,000 contractors, raised a $30 million seed round led by Peak XV.
key_facts.excerpt: Maxinsights, which creates training data for robots using first-person footage from cameras worn by 5,000+ contractors, raised a $30M seed led by Peak XV (John Koetsier/Forbes)
